name: io_cancel
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_io_cancel, aio_context_t ctx_id, struct iocb *iocb, struct io_event *result);
description: The io_cancel() system call attempts to cancel an asynchronous I/O operation previously submitted with io_submit(2). It uses the AIO context and the I/O control block to identify the operation. If successful, the event is copied to the specified result without being placed in the completion queue.

parameters.name: ctx_id
parameters.description: The AIO context to which the operation was submitted.

parameters.name: iocb
parameters.description: Pointer to the I/O control block describing the operation to be canceled.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Pointer to the memory where the result event will be copied if the operation is canceled.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The iocb specified was not canceled.
One of the data structures points to invalid data.
The AIO context specified by ctx_id is invalid.
io_cancel() is not implemented on this architecture.
